title: Converged embeddings SDK: deterministic pagination, typed payloads, and deterministic retries
creator: Marcus Lee
description: Standardize and harden the Embeddings client surface across Python and TypeScript SDKs. Deliver deterministic pagination cursors, a typed response contract for both languages, and idempotent retry semantics to enable safe resumable requests and predictable client behavior under load. Goals: (1) reduce developer confusion from divergent SDKs, (2) decrease tail latency for large paginated workloads via prefetching and controlled backpressure, (3) improve error clarity and automated resume capabilities for client apps.
acceptance_criteria: New SDKs expose a single pagination API (page_cursor + iterator) with opaque deterministic cursors documented in the spec
Typed response interfaces provided for TypeScript and dataclass/TypedDict shapes for Python with unit tests covering schema validation
Retry semantics are idempotent: clients can safely retry up to N seconds using idempotency token + cursor; server-side guarantees documented
Benchmarked 95th and 99th percentile latency improvement of paginated embedding workloads (target: >= 15% improvement vs current client)
Backward compatibility: old query parameters still accepted and a deprecation notice published (deprecation window >= 3 months)
End-to-end tests in CI exercising resume after transient 429/503 and verifying no-duplicate embeddings semantics
technical_details: Cursor format: base64( version || stream_id || seq_no || sha256(prefix_vector) ) — opaque to user but deterministic for identical prefix inputs
Resumability: server accepts cursor + idempotency_token; if token omitted, client falls back to last-known-seq semantics (best-effort resume, may duplicate up to page_size items)

Pagination contract: SDK exposes two helpers: fetch_page(cursor, page_size) -> (items[], next_cursor) and iterate_embeddings(page_size, prefetch=1) async/iterator that maintains one prefetch window to hide network latency

Typed responses: TypeScript interface EmbeddingPage<T> { items: T[]; nextCursor: string | null; meta: PageMeta } and Python dataclass EmbeddingPage with typed fields and runtime validation for CI-only tests

Retry mapping: 429 -> BackoffRetry with exponential jitter; 503 -> Circuit-aware retry (bounded retries + open-circuit escalation); 500 -> No automatic retry except idempotent replays flagged by idempotency_token

Backpressure and batching: client implements dynamic windowing: start window=1, increase on success to max_window=3 for low-latency consumers, and reduce on timeouts/503s; this limits memory usage while improving throughput

Compatibility: server will accept legacy offset-based pagination (?cursor=legacy-offset) and translate to new cursors for the deprecation period; SDKs will expose a migration helper: convert_legacy_cursor(legacy) -> new_cursor
Observability hooks: SDK emits structured telemetry events (page_requested, page_received, cursor_resume_attempt) with counters suitable for Console dashboards and alerts
Security note: cursors are opaque but include a short HMAC to detect tampering; HMAC key rotation handled server-side, clients remain unchanged
notes: Trade-offs considered: embedding checksum in the cursor increases cursor size but enables deterministic resumes for identical prefixes (preferred for dedup and resume correctness)
We evaluated two approaches for prefetch: aggressive prefetch (window=5) vs conservative (window<=3). Chosen conservative to reduce bursty memory/CPU when many clients prefetch simultaneously.
Typed runtime validation is enabled in CI tests only to avoid shipping heavy runtime dep in production Python SDK; runtime lightweight checks (typing-based assertions) remain optional for end users

Decision: expose idempotency_token in client constructor and request-level override. Default behavior: auto-generate per-iterator session token to make short-lived retries safe without user intervention.

comments: 2026-02-26 Marcus Lee: Kickoff — scoped work to SDK parity and server cursor contract. Created initial PoC for TS iterator; results looked promising under synthetic load.

2026-03-02 Anita Chowdhury: Ran cluster benchmark with 128 concurrent iterators, page_size=64. Observed 18% P95 latency reduction with prefetch=1 and 26% reduction in average total wall-time for full corpus scans compared to legacy offset pagination.
2026-03-03 Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria, asked for explicit deprecation plan for legacy cursor and customer communication timeline. Assigned docs action item.

2026-03-04 Ethan Kim (Design): API ergonomics review — requested smaller surface area for beginners: provide a simple.iterate_embeddings(...) default wrapper and advanced low-level fetch_page for power users. Agreed.
2026-03-05 Security: Verified HMAC approach is acceptable; request to add key-rotation note and server-side audit trail. Security will run a short audit before release.
2026-03-06 QA: Integration tests flapping on 503 handling — discovered bug in backoff jitter implementation (fixed in PR #1124). Added deterministic seeds in CI to make flaky timing tests stable.
2026-03-07 Anita Chowdhury: Merged Python draft; running canary against internal embeddings dataset (100M tokens). No duplication observed after resume with idempotency token in 10k resume scenarios.
2026-03-08 Marcus Lee: Blocking item — need final sign-off from infra on circuit metadata exposure (will require small schema change to API response headers). Raised ENG-57955 to track infra change.
qa_plan: Unit tests for cursor encode/decode and tamper detection
E2E test: simulate network partition and resume, verify no duplicates beyond page_size (for non-idempotent tokens document expected behavior)
Load test: 1k concurrent iterators with mixed page_size (8, 32, 64) and measure P50/P95/P99, memory, and CPU
Compatibility test: legacy cursor conversion helper validated against historical cursor logs
CI gating: require green on integration suite and perf benchmarks not regressing more than 5% on P95
